contents.html_ja: SCAP 仕様は、SCAP の構成要素と、SCAP の文脈でそれらが互いにどう関係するかを特定しています。ただし、SCAP 仕様は SCAP の構成要素そのものを定義するものではなく、各構成要素には独立した仕様があります。SCAP の構成要素は、MITRE Corporation、国家安全保障局（NSA）、Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams（FIRST）などの複数の組織が作成し、維持しています。
contents.html: The SCAP specification identifies the SCAP components and how they relate to each other within the context of SCAP. However, the SCAP specification does not define the SCAP components themselves; each component has its own standalone specification. The SCAP components were created and are maintained by several entities, including the MITRE Corporation, the National Security Agency (NSA), and the Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams (FIRST).

To manage that evolution, a timeline has been constructed to balance progress against stability:

contents.html_ja: 仕様には、本質的な価値と相乗的な価値の両方があります。仕様は、それ自体の長所で価値を示すという意味で、本質的な価値を持ちます。たとえば、XCCDF はチェックリストの内容を表現する標準的な方法です。XCCDF は、CPE、CCE、OVAL などの他の仕様と組み合わせて、SCAP 検証済み製品が処理できる SCAP で表現されたチェックリストを作成することで、相乗的な価値も持ちます。同様に CVE は、追跡のために脆弱性を列挙する一貫した方法というだけでも利用事例がありますが、CPE や OVAL と組み合わせることで、SCAP 検証済み製品が処理できる、脆弱性の自動化されたチェックというより大きな利用事例を形成するところまで高められます。これらの関係は NIST SP 800-126 に記載されています。ただし、仕様は SCAP の仕様でなくても、それ自体で価値を示せるし、示すべきであることを認識することが重要です。これに対処するため、NIST は、個々の仕様について別個の、しかし関連する検証プログラムを実施する可能性を探ります。たとえば NIST は、SCAP の利用事例では使われない可能性のある OVAL の機能について製品を試験できるようにする目的で、OVAL 検証プログラムを実施する過程にあります。
contents.html: Specifications have both intrinsic and synergistic value. They have intrinsic value in that the specification demonstrates value on its own merits. For example, XCCDF is a standard way of expressing checklist content. XCCDF also has a synergistic value when combined with other specifications such as CPE, CCE, and OVAL to create an SCAP-expressed checklist that can be processed by SCAP-validated products. Likewise, CVE has use cases in simply being a consistent way to enumerate vulnerabilities for tracking purposes; however, when combined with CPE and OVAL, CVE is elevated to formulate a greater use case, namely that of automated checks for vulnerabilities that can be processed by SCAP-validated products. These relationships are captured in NIST SP 800-126. However, it is important to recognize that specifications can and should demonstrate value in their own right without being SCAP specifications. To address this, NIST will explore the possibility of implementing separate but related validation programs for individual specifications. For example, NIST is in the process of implementing an OVAL Validation program with the purpose of allowing products to be tested for OVAL functionality that may not be used in SCAP use cases.

contents.html_ja: 利用者のコンピュータに対する脅威は、リモートから仕掛けられるネットワークサービスの悪用から、電子メール、悪意のある Web サイト、感染したファイルのダウンロードを通じて拡散する悪意のあるコードまで、数多くあります。IT 製品の脆弱性は毎日発見されており、すぐに使える多くの悪用技法がインターネット上で広く入手できます。IT 製品は幅広い層の利用者を想定していることが多いため、制限的なセキュリティ構成の管理策は通常、デフォルトでは有効にされておらず、箱から出したままの多くの IT 製品は直ちに脆弱になります。加えて、多くの IT 製品について合理的なセキュリティ設定の集合を特定することは、経験豊富なシステム管理者にとっても、複雑で骨が折れ、時間のかかる作業です。
contents.html: There are many threats to users’ computers, ranging from remotely launched network service exploits to malicious code spread through e-mails, malicious websites, and download of infected files. Vulnerabilities in IT products are discovered daily, and many ready-to-use exploitation techniques are widely available on the Internet. Because IT products are often intended for a wide variety of audiences, restrictive security configuration controls are usually not enabled by default, so many out-of-the-box IT products are immediately vulnerable. In addition, identifying a reasonable set of security settings for many IT products is a complicated, arduous, and time-consuming task, even for experienced system administrators.

contents.html_ja: チェックリストには、セキュリティ構成を自動的に設定または検証できるファイルなど、さまざまな形があります。自動化された方法を持つことは、いくつもの理由から、ますます重要になっています。その理由には、さまざまな法律、大統領令、指令、ポリシー、規則、標準、ガイダンスへの準拠を達成する複雑さ、情報システムの脆弱性の増加、それらの脆弱性を狙う脅威の高度化があります。自動化により、セキュリティ管理策と構成設定が情報システム内で一貫して適用され、管理策と設定を効果的に検証できるようになります。
contents.html: Checklists can take many forms, including files that can automatically set or verify security configurations. Having automated methods has become increasingly important for several reasons, including the complexity of achieving compliance with various laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidance; the increasing number of vulnerabilities in information systems; and the growing sophistication of threats against those vulnerabilities. Automation ensures that the security controls and configuration settings are applied consistently within an information system, and that the controls and settings can be effectively verified.

contents.html_ja: SCAP プログラムは、標準に基づくセキュリティツールが NCP のチェックリストを使って構成チェックを自動的に実行できるようにすることで、こうしたニーズに対応します。セキュリティ製品とチェックリストの作成者は、SCAP のデータリポジトリから内容を組み立てて、実用的な SCAP で表現されたセキュリティガイダンスを作成します。望ましいセキュリティ構成設定、インストールされたパッチ、その他のシステムのセキュリティ要素を、標準化された形式の SCAP を用いて文書化したセキュリティ構成チェックリストは、SCAP で表現されたチェックリストと呼ばれます。そのようなチェックリストは、チェックリストの記述に XCCDF を、対処または評価するセキュリティ構成設定の識別に CCE を、チェックリストが有効なプラットフォームの識別に CPE を使います。XCCDF のチェックリスト内での CCE と CPE の項目の使用は、SCAP の規約（有効な SCAP の使用のための要件）の一例です（詳細は NIST SP 800-126 を参照）。SCAP の規約のもう 1 つの例は、チェックリスト内の個々のチェックを、NIST SP 800-53、Recommended Security Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations のセキュリティ管理策などの外部の要件にマッピングすることです。SCAP の内容を作成する組織は、最高度の相互運用性を確保するため、これらの規約に従うべきです。
contents.html: The SCAP program addresses these needs by enabling standards-based security tools to automatically perform configuration checking using NCP checklists. Security products and checklist authors assemble content from SCAP data repositories to create viable SCAP-expressed security guidance. A security configuration checklist that documents desired security configuration settings, installed patches, and other system security elements using SCAP in a standardized format is known as an SCAP-expressed checklist. Such a checklist would use XCCDF to describe the checklist, CCE to identify security configuration settings to be addressed or assessed, and CPE to identify platforms for which the checklist is valid. The use of CCE and CPE entries within XCCDF checklists is an example of an SCAP convention — a requirement for valid SCAP usage (See NIST SP 800-126 for more information.) Another example of an SCAP convention is the mapping of individual checks within a checklist to external requirements such as security controls from NIST SP 800-53, Recommended Security Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations. Organizations producing SCAP content should adhere to these conventions to ensure the highest degree of interoperability.

contents.html: There are 128 checklists posted on the website; 17 of the checklists are SCAP-expressed and can be used with SCAP-validated products. It is anticipated that a minimum of 26 more SCAP-expressed checklists will be added in FY2010 as contributions come from other federal agencies and product vendors. This allows organizations to use checklists obtained from the NCP website (checklists.nist.gov) for automated security configuration patch assessment. NCP currently hosts SCAP checklists for Internet Explorer 7.0, Office 2007, Red Hat Linux, Symantec AntiVirus, Windows 2000, Windows 2003 Server, Windows Vista, Windows XP and other products.

contents.html: To assist users in identifying automated checklist content, NCP groups checklists into tiers, from tier I to tier IV as in Figure 2 on the previous page. NCP uses the tiers to rank checklists according to their automation capability. Tier IV checklists are considered production-ready and have been validated by NIST SP 800-70 Revision 1, National Checklist Program for IT Products—Guidelines for Checklist Users and Developers, to ensure, to the maximum extent possible, interoperability with SCAP-validated products. Tier III checklists have not been validated, but they can be executed by SCAP-validated products. Tier II checklists document recommended security settings in a machine-readable, non-standard format, such as a proprietary format or a product-specific configuration script. Tier I checklists are prose-based and contain no machine-readable content.
contents.html_ja: 利用者が自動化されたチェックリストの内容を特定するのを支援するため、NCP はチェックリストを、前のページの図 2 にあるように、ティア I からティア IV に分類しています。NCP は、チェックリストを自動化の能力に従ってランク付けするためにティアを使っています。ティア IV のチェックリストは本番利用が可能と見なされ、SCAP 検証済み製品との相互運用性を可能な限り確保するため、NIST SP 800-70 Revision 1、National Checklist Program for IT Products—Guidelines for Checklist Users and Developers により検証されています。ティア III のチェックリストは検証されていませんが、SCAP 検証済み製品で実行できます。ティア II のチェックリストは、推奨されるセキュリティ設定を、独自形式や製品固有の構成スクリプトなど、機械可読だが標準ではない形式で文書化しています。ティア I のチェックリストは散文ベースで、機械可読な内容を含みません。

contents.html_ja: チェックリストは、デフォルトではティア IV からティア I の順に並べられています。利用者は、チェックリストのティア、IT 製品、IT 製品のカテゴリ、権威者によってチェックリストを閲覧でき、また、利用者が指定した用語をチェックリストの名称と要約から探すキーワード検索でも閲覧できます。検索結果には、チェックリストの詳細なメタデータと、そのチェックリストの SCAP の内容へのリンク、およびチェックリストに関連する支援資料へのリンクが表示されます。
contents.html: Checklists are sorted by default according to tier, from tier IV to tier I. Users can browse the checklists based on the checklist tier, IT product, IT product category, or authority, and also through a keyword search that searches the checklist name and summary for user-specified terms. The search results show the detailed checklist metadata and a link to any SCAP content for the checklist, as well as links to any supporting resources associated with the checklist.

contents.html: Although checklists are encouraged for use in both the private and public sectors, federal agencies are required to use security configuration checklists from the NCP. In February 2008, revised Part 39 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) was published. Paragraph (d) of section 39.101 states, “In acquiring information technology, agencies shall include the appropriate IT security policies and requirements, including use of common security configurations available from the NIST website at http://checklists.nist.gov. Agency contracting officers should consult with the requiring official to ensure the appropriate standards are incorporated.” In Memorandum M08-22, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) mandated the use of SCAP Validated products for continuous monitoring of Federal Desktop Core Configuration (FDCC) compliance.

contents.html_ja: セキュリティコンテンツ自動化プロトコル（SCAP）検証プログラムは、製品が SCAP を正しく実装していることを確保するために、適合性試験を行います。適合性試験が必要なのは、SCAP がさまざまな利用事例を満たすために連携して動作する 6 つの個別の仕様からなる、複雑な仕様だからです。製品の実装における 1 つの誤りが、機関や産業界のネットワーク内で、脆弱性やポリシー不適合が検出されないままになる結果につながる可能性があります。
contents.html: The Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP) Validation Program performs conformance testing to ensure that products correctly implement SCAP. Conformance testing is necessary because SCAP is a complex specification consisting of six individual specifications that work together to meet various use cases. A single error in product implementation could result in undetected vulnerabilities or policy non-compliance within agency and industry networks.

contents.html_ja: SCAP 検証プログラムは、連邦デスクトップ標準構成（FDCC）を支えるため、OMB の要請により作られました。このプログラムは、NIST の全米試験所認定プログラム（NVLAP）と連携して、NISTIR 7511 Revision 1 の草案、Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP) Version 1.0 Validation Program Test Requirements に基づいて試験を実施する独立の適合性試験所を設置します。試験が完了すると、試験所は試験報告書を NIST に提出してレビューと承認を受けます。製品の検証は現在 1 年間有効で、その時点でベンダーは、製品を試験に提出することで検証を更新できます。SCAP 検証試験は、安価でありながら効果的であるよう設計されています。SCAP の適合性試験は、人間が容易に検証できるか、NIST が提供する参照ツールで自動化されています。これまでにプログラムは、10 の独立の試験所を認定し、19 のベンダーの 25 製品を検証しました。
contents.html: The SCAP Validation Program was created on request by the OMB to support the Federal Desktop Core Configuration (FDCC). It works with the NIST National Voluntary Laboratory Accreditation Program (NVLAP) to set up independent conformance testing laboratories that conduct the testing based on draft NISTIR 7511 Revision 1, Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP) Version 1.0 Validation Program Test Requirements. When testing is completed, the laboratory submits a test report to NIST for review and approval. Product validations are currently active for one year, at which time vendors have the option to renew their validation by submitting the product for testing. SCAP validation testing has been designed to be inexpensive, yet effective. The SCAP conformance tests are either easily human verifiable or automated through NIST provided reference tools. To date, the program has accredited ten independent laboratories and validated 25 products from 19 different vendors.

contents.html: While FDCC SCAP testing is an important part of the program, it is only one of several SCAP capabilities which vendors can apply to test their products. The others cover product capabilities such as configuration scanning, vulnerability scanning, patch checking, and remediation capabilities, all within the SCAP context.

This procurement mandates SCAP validation for participating products and was publically announced on July 15, 2009. The Department of Defense (DOD) Computer Network Defense (CND) initiative also relies of SCAP validation for the future DOD cyber security strategy.

contents.html_ja: もう 1 つの新しい分野は、現在は初期段階にある SCAP コンテンツ検証プログラムです。その目的は、国家チェックリストプログラム（NCP）を通じて提供される SCAP コンテンツが、同じ利用事例の SCAP 検証製品で確実に動作するよう保証することです。SCAP の利用がミッションクリティカルな領域へと拡大し続けるなかで、この技術の利用者が、期待どおりに機能することを確信できることはますます重要になっています。これは、SCAP コンテンツが SCAP 検証済み製品で処理されるとき、エラーなく動作すべきであることを意味します。この目標を達成するには、SCAP コンテンツ検証プログラムの創設が必要です。SCAP 製品検証プログラムと NCP とともに実施される SCAP コンテンツ検証は、構成コンプライアンスなどの特定の利用事例を満たすよう設計されたコンテンツが、同じ利用事例について SCAP 検証済み製品によって完全かつ正確に処理できることを確保します。NCP は、ティア構造を用いて、SCAP 検証済みコンテンツを最上位のティア IV に置くことで目立たせます（http://csrc.nist.gov の NIST SP 800-70 Rev 1 を参照）。これにより、エンドユーザーは、必要なコンテンツを迅速かつ簡単に特定し、SCAP 検証済み製品と組み合わせて、任務上の目標を達成できます。
contents.html: Another new area, currently in its early stages, is the SCAP Content Validation Program. Its purpose will be to ensure that SCAP content is available through the National Checklist Program (NCP) is assured to work in SCAP Validation Products within the same use case. As the use of SCAP continues to grow into mission critical areas, it is increasingly important that users of the technology can be assured that it will function as expected. This means that when SCAP content is processed by a SCAP validated product, it should work without error. Achieving this goal requires the creation of the SCAP Content Validation Program. Carried out in conjunction with the SCAP Product Validation Program and the NCP, SCAP Content Validation will ensure that content designed to meet a specific use case, such as configuration compliance, can be processed fully and accurately by SCAP validated products for that same use case. The NCP, using a tiered structure, will highlight SCAP validated content by placing it in the highest tier, Tier IV (See NIST SP 800-70 Rev 1 at http://csrc.nist.gov.) This provides end users a fast and simple way to identify the content they need, pair it with their SCAP validated products, and achieve their mission goals.

contents.html_ja: 測定は、あらゆる科学分野で大きな進歩を遂げるための鍵であり、コンピュータセキュリティも例外ではありません。測定は、セキュリティの特性を表現する標準化された方法を与えてくれます。脅威、脆弱性、緩和戦略の複雑さが増し続けているため、攻撃、脆弱性、セキュリティ管理策の測定に関する追加の研究が特に強く必要とされています。これらの分野の測定能力が向上すれば、組織は、セキュリティ管理策を計画、実装、構成する際に、科学的に妥当な判断を下せるようになります。これにより、セキュリティ管理策の有効性が向上し、不要で効果のない管理策を排除することで費用も削減されます。
contents.html: Measurement is the key to making major advancements in any scientific field, and computer security is no exception. Measures give us a standardized way of expressing security characteristics. Because of the ever-increasing complexity of threats, vulnerabilities, and mitigation strategies, there is a particularly strong need for additional research on attack, vulnerability, and security control measurement. Improved measurement capabilities in these areas would allow organizations to make scientifically sound decisions when planning, implementing, and configuring security controls. This would improve the effectiveness of security controls, while reducing cost by eliminating unnecessary, ineffective controls.

contents.html: In FY2009, CSD continued its long-term research efforts on technical security metrics, focused primarily on attack, vulnerability, and security control measurement. The first stage of this work involves developing specifications for measuring and scoring individual vulnerabilities, and researching how vulnerabilities from multiple hosts can be used in sequence to compromise particular targets. A summary of these efforts from the past year is presented below. NIST also released NISTIR 7564, Directions in Security Metrics Research, in April 2009. NISTIR 7564 provides an overview of the security metrics area and looks at possible avenues of research that could be pursued to advance the state of the art.

contents.html: Network Security Analysis Using Attack Graphs

contents.html_ja: 現在、コンピュータネットワークは、電力網、金融データシステム、緊急通信システムなどの分野で、IT 基盤の中核的な構成要素となっています。これらのネットワークを悪意のある侵入から保護することは、国の経済と安全保障にとって極めて重要です。これらのネットワーク化されたシステムのセキュリティを向上させるには、異なるネットワーク構成によって提供されるセキュリティの量を測定する必要があります。当部門の研究の目的は、コンピュータネットワークのセキュリティを測定する標準モデルを開発することです。標準モデルにより、「昨日より安全になったか」や「あるネットワーク構成のセキュリティは別の構成と比べてどうか」といった問いに答えられるようになります。また、ネットワークセキュリティを測定する標準モデルがあれば、利用者、ベンダー、研究者が一堂に会して、ネットワークセキュリティの方法論と製品を評価できるようになります。
contents.html: At present, computer networks constitute the core component of IT infrastructures in areas such as power grids, financial data systems, and emergency communication systems. Protection of these networks from malicious intrusions is critical to the economy and security of our nation. To improve the security of these networked systems, it is necessary to measure the amount of security provided by different network configurations. The objective of our research is to develop a standard model for measuring the security of computer networks. A standard model will enable us to answer questions such as “are we more secure than yesterday” or “how does the security of one network configuration compare with another one”. Also, having a standard model to measure network security will bring together users, vendors, and researchers to evaluate methodologies and products for network security.

contents.html: Good metrics should be measured consistently; they are inexpensive to collect, are expressed numerically, have units of measure, and have specific context. We meet this challenge by capturing vulnerability interdependencies and measuring security in the exact way that real attackers penetrate the network. Our methodology for security risk analysis is based on the model of attack graphs. We analyze all attack paths through a network, providing a probabilistic metric of the overall system risk. Through this metric, we analyze tradeoffs between security costs and security benefits. Our metric is consistent, unambiguous, and provides context for understanding security risk of computer networks.
contents.html_ja: 優れた測定指標は、一貫して測定され、収集に費用がかからず、数値で表現され、測定の単位を持ち、特定の文脈を持ちます。当部門は、脆弱性の相互依存性を捉え、現実の攻撃者がネットワークに侵入するまさにその方法でセキュリティを測定することで、この課題に対応しています。当部門のセキュリティリスク分析の方法論は、攻撃グラフのモデルに基づいています。ネットワーク内のすべての攻撃経路を分析し、システム全体のリスクの確率的な測定指標を提供します。この測定指標を通じて、セキュリティのコストとセキュリティの便益のトレードオフを分析します。当部門の測定指標は一貫していて曖昧さがなく、コンピュータネットワークのセキュリティリスクを理解するための文脈を提供します。

contents.html_ja: FY2009 に当部門は、ベイジアンネットワークに基づく新しいセキュリティ分析のモデルを開発しました。これには、自動化された脆弱性スキャンツールが利用可能で広く使われていることと、攻撃グラフを構築する新しい種類のアルゴリズムが必要でした。また、当部門の方法が数千台のホストからなるエンタープライズネットワークにどのように拡張できるかを理解するため、当部門の技法の性能分析も行いました。この作業に基づく多数の論文が、カンファレンスやワークショップで発表されました。FY2010 には、「ゼロデイ攻撃」など、これまで知られていなかった種類の悪用を扱えるよう技法を強化する計画です。また、結果をカンファレンスや学術誌で発表する計画です。
contents.html: In FY2009, we developed a new model of security analysis based on Bayesian Networks. This required the availability and widespread use of automated vulnerability scanning tools, and a new type of algorithm to construct attack graphs. We also did performance analysis of our techniques to understand how our method will scale up for enterprise networks consisting of several thousand hosts. Numerous papers were published in conferences and workshops based on this work. In FY2010, we plan to enhance our techniques to handle previously unknown types of exploits, such as “zero day attacks”. We also plan to publish our results in conferences and journals.

contents.html: Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) and Internet Protocol Security (IPsec)

contents.html_ja: インターネットプロトコルバージョン 6（IPv6）は、現在のインターネットプロトコルである IPv4 の改訂版です。IPv6 は、Internet Engineering Task Force（IETF）により、一連のコンセンサスに基づく標準文書、すなわち承認された標準文書である Requests for Comment（RFC）と、標準になる可能性のある作業中の文書である Internet Drafts（ID）で、策定され定義されており、今後も続きます。これらの文書は、アプリケーションから物理層まで、ネットワークスタックのあらゆる階層でのネットワーク通信の内容と動作を定義しています。
contents.html: The Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) is an updated version of the current Internet Protocol, IPv4. It has been, and continues to be, developed and defined by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) in a series of consensus-based standards documents—Requests for Comment (RFCs), which are approved standards documents, and Internet Drafts (IDs), which are works-in-progress that may progress to become standards. These documents define the contents and behavior of network communications at every level of the networking stack, from applications down to the physical layer.

contents.html_ja: IPv6 が開発された主な動機は、一意の IP アドレスの数を増やすことと、新しいインターネットアプリケーションや機器のニーズに対応することでした。加えて IPv6 は、ネットワークの管理と構成の容易さの向上、拡張可能な IP ヘッダ、モビリティとセキュリティの改善、サービス品質の制御という目標を持って設計されました。
contents.html: The primary motivations for the development of IPv6 were to increase the number of unique IP addresses and to handle the needs of new Internet applications and devices. In addition, IPv6 was designed with the following goals: increased ease of network management and configuration, expandable IP headers, improved mobility and security, and quality of service controls.

contents.html_ja: 米国 OMB は、政府機関が 2008 年までにバックボーンシステム（ルータ、ゲートウェイなど）に IPv6 の能力を組み込むよう義務付けました。NIST の職員は、政府機関が相互運用可能で安全な方法で移行を計画し実行するのを支援するために設置された、連邦の IPv6 作業部会に積極的に参加しました。また、IPv6 のどの部分と機能が政府機関にとって必須で、どれが任意であり、それらの要素がどこで正確に定義されているかを定義する、IPv6 プロファイルも作成しました。
contents.html: The U.S. OMB mandated that government agencies should incorporate IPv6 capability into their backbone systems (routers, gateways, etc.) by 2008. NIST personnel actively participated in the federal IPv6 Working Group, formed to help government agencies plan and execute the transition in an interoperable and secure manner. We also developed an IPv6 profile to define which pieces and features of IPv6 are mandatory for government agencies, which are optional, and where these elements are precisely defined.

contents.html_ja: インターネットプロトコルセキュリティ（IPsec）は、IP ネットワーク上の私的な通信を確保するためのオープンな標準のフレームワークであり、最も普及しているネットワーク層のセキュリティ管理策になっています。IPSec は、機密性、完全性、データ出所認証、パケットのリプレイとトラフィック分析の防止、アクセス制御など、いくつかの種類のデータ保護を提供できます。IPsec は通常、IPsec 接続の設定をネゴシエートし、鍵を交換し、エンドポイントを相互に認証し、IPsec で保護された接続のセキュリティを定義するセキュリティアソシエーションを確立するために、Internet Key Exchange（IKE）プロトコルを使います。IPsec と IKE は、IPv4 がしばらく展開された後に追加されましたが、現在ではすべての主要なオペレーティングシステムに統合されています。IPv6 では、IPsec と IKE はネットワークプロトコルの不可欠な部分となる予定です。
contents.html: Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) is a framework of open standards for ensuring private communications over IP networks, which has become the most popular network layer security control. IPSec can provide several types of data protection—confidentiality; integrity; data origin authentication; prevention of packet replay and traffic analysis; and access control. IPsec typically uses the Internet Key Exchange (IKE) protocol to negotiate IPsec connection settings, exchange keys, authenticate endpoints to each other, and establish security associations, which define the security of IPsec protected connections. IPsec and IKE were added to IPv4 after it had been deployed for some time, but are now integrated into all of the major operating systems. For IPv6, IPsec and IKE are planned to be an integral part of the network protocols.

contents.html_ja: IPsec にはいくつかの用途があり、最も一般的なのは仮想プライベートネットワーク（VPN）です。これは、既存の物理ネットワークの上に構築される仮想ネットワークで、ネットワーク間で送信されるデータと IP 情報に、安全な通信メカニズムを提供できます。VPN はネットワーキングのリスクを減らせますが、完全になくすことはできません。たとえば、仮想プライベートネットワーク（VPN）の実装には、アルゴリズムやソフトウェアの欠陥、または攻撃者が悪用できる安全でない構成設定や値があるかもしれません。
contents.html: IPsec has several uses, with the most common being a virtual private network (VPN). This is a virtual network built on top of existing physical networks that can provide a secure communications mechanism for data and IP information transmitted between networks. Although VPNs can reduce the risks of networking, they cannot totally eliminate them. For example, a virtual private network (VPN) implementation may have flaws in algorithms or software, or insecure configuration settings and values that attackers can exploit.

contents.html_ja: NIST SP 500-267、A Profile for IPv6 in the United States Government (USG) - Version 1.0, は 2008 年 7 月に発行されました。この文書は、連邦機関が IPv6 を実装した製品を調達し展開する計画を策定するのを支援するプロファイルです。このプロファイルは、ホスト、ルータ、侵入検知システム、ファイアウォールなどの一般的なネットワーク機器について IPv6 の能力を推奨し、ほとんどの連邦機関の最低限の運用要件を満たすために必要な IPv6 の標準と仕様の選択を含んでいます。IPv6 に対応した連邦情報システムが相互運用可能で安全であることを確保するのに役立つよう作成されたこの刊行物は、そうしたシステムが現在の IPv4 システムとどのように相互運用し共存できるかを扱っています。固有の情報技術要件を持つ機関は、NIST のプロファイルを、さらに精緻化された仕様とポリシーの基礎として使うことが期待されます。
contents.html: NIST SP 500-267, A Profile for IPv6 in the United States Government (USG) - Version 1.0, was published in July 2008. This document is a profile to assist federal agencies in developing plans to acquire and deploy products that implement IPv6. The profile recommends IPv6 capabilities for common network devices, including hosts, routers, intrusion detection systems, and firewalls, and includes a selection of IPv6 standards and specifications needed to meet the minimum operational requirements of most federal agencies. Developed to help ensure that IPv6-enabled federal information systems are interoperable and secure, the publication addresses how such systems can interoperate and coexist with the current IPv4 systems. Agencies with unique information technology requirements are expected to use the NIST profile as a basis for further refined specifications and policies.

contents.html_ja: OMB Memorandum 05-22（OMB の URL: http://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/memoranda/fy2005/m05-22.pdf）で、NIST は IPv6 への準拠を扱う標準の策定を課されました。連邦政府における IPv6 の技術要件を規定するため、USG v6 プロファイル（USGv6 Profile: http://www.antd.nist.gov/usgv6/profile.html）が発行されました。この文書で当部門は、IPv6 の初期採用者の信頼を確保し投資を保護するために、製品試験サービスが必要になる可能性が高いことを示唆しています。既存の試験プログラムを調査し、USG 独自の試験プログラムが必要であると結論付けましたが、USG の技術要件とプロファイリング要件に対応できる、利用者／ベンダーの幅広い協働の試験イニシアチブへの調和と収斂にコミットすることを前提としています。
contents.html: In OMB Memorandum 05-22 (OMB URL: http://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/memoranda/fy2005/m05-22.pdf ) NIST is tasked to develop a standard that addresses compliance with IPv6. The USG v6 Profile (USGv6 Profile: http://www.antd.nist.gov/usgv6/profile.html) has been published to specify the technical requirements for IPv6 in the federal government. In that document we suggest that product testing services are likely to be needed to ensure the confidence and to protect the investment of early IPv6 adopters. We surveyed the existing testing programs and concluded that a distinct USG testing program is needed, but with the commitment to harmonization and convergence into a broad collaborative user/vendor testing initiative, which can accommodate the technical and profiling requirements of the USG.

contents.html: In order to promote confidence and mutual recognition of test results, we added the requirement for test results to be developed at laboratories that are accredited for these test methods in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025. The accreditation landscape has itself changed in recent years. Where it was once possible to designate a single, usually government-run accrediting authority, there is now competition from private accreditors who compete on a level playing field. The qualifications for laboratory accreditation organizations include compliance with ISO/IEC 17011, and being signatory to the International Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation (ILAC) Mutual Recognition Agreement (MRA). In order to promote comparability of test results across the accredited testing laboratories, we encourage qualified accreditors to collaborate in the development of IPV6 testing specific accreditation requirements and to publish or reference the technical criteria to be applied in addition to the requirements of ISO/IEC 17025 in the accreditation of IPV6 testing laboratories. NIST SP 500-273, USGv6 Test Methods: General Description and Validation, was developed to provide guidance to all accreditors and test laboratories on units of accreditation, standard reference tests, test method validation criteria, and vital feedback mechanisms to maintain quality improvement in test suites, in addition to maintaining consistency of test interpretations.
contents.html_ja: 試験結果の信頼性と相互承認を促進するため、試験結果を、これらの試験方法について ISO/IEC 17025 に従って認定された試験所で得ることを要件に加えました。認定をめぐる状況自体も、近年変化しています。かつては、通常は政府が運営する単一の認定機関を指定できましたが、現在は対等な条件で競争する民間の認定機関との競争があります。試験所認定機関の資格には、ISO/IEC 17011 への準拠と、International Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation（ILAC）Mutual Recognition Agreement（MRA）の署名機関であることが含まれます。認定された試験所間で試験結果の比較可能性を促進するため、資格のある認定機関に、IPV6 の試験に固有の認定要件の策定で協力し、IPV6 試験所の認定において ISO/IEC 17025 の要件に加えて適用される技術基準を公表または参照するよう奨励しています。NIST SP 500-273、USGv6 Test Methods: General Description and Validation は、試験解釈の一貫性を維持することに加え、認定の単位、標準の参照試験、試験方法の検証基準、試験スイートの品質改善を維持するための重要なフィードバックメカニズムについて、すべての認定機関と試験所にガイダンスを提供するために作成されました。

contents.html: Testing of network protection devices requires a separate infrastructure. It involves functional testing, local interface, environment, and document inspection.

contents.html_ja: USGv6 プロファイルへの準拠の主張は、サポートされる USGv6 の能力と、認定試験所による各能力の試験結果を詳述した Supplier's Declaration of Conformity（SDoC）を用いて文書化しなければなりません。この方式では、製品は認定試験所で適合性と相互運用性について試験され、試験結果と USGv6 文書の要件のレビューに基づいて、供給者は、製品が何であるか、その仕様、同等の機器、サポートされる上位レベルのカテゴリを記録した SDoC を発行します。供給者の宣言の標準化された形式は、IPV6 の試験と適合性評価に対するこの手法の受入れを促進します。
contents.html: Claims of compliance with the USGv6 profile shall be documented using a Supplier's Declaration of Conformity (SDoC) which details the USGv6 capabilities supported and the results of testing each capability by an accredited laboratory. In this scheme, the product is tested for conformance and interoperability in accredited laboratories; based on a review of the test results and the requirements of the USGv6 document, the supplier issues an SDoC recording what the product is, its specifications, equivalent machines, and the high level categories supported. A standardized format for the supplier's declaration will promote the acceptance of this approach to testing and conformity assessment of IPV6.

contents.html: NIST SP 800-119, Guidelines for the Secure Deployment of IPv6, will be posted for public comment in FY2010. New sections were added to address late-breaking, significant changes in the approach to IPv6 transition.

contents.html_ja: ドメインネームシステム（DNS）は、http://csrc.nist.gov のような覚えやすい形のインターネットアドレスを、129.6.13.39 のような同等の数値のインターネットプロトコル（IP）アドレスに変換する、世界規模の分散システムです。世界中の特定のサーバが、必要なデータベースを維持し、変換も行います。変換を行う DNS サーバは、アドレスの変換に必要なデータを自身で持っていない場合、インターネット上の他の DNS サーバと通信することがあります。
contents.html: The Domain Name System (DNS) is a global distributed system in which Internet addresses in mnemonic form such as http://csrc.nist.gov are converted into the equivalent numeric Internet Protocol (IP) addresses such as 129.6.13.39. Certain servers throughout the world maintain the databases needed, as well as perform the translations. A DNS server that is performing a translation may communicate with other Internet DNS servers if it does not have the data needed to translate the address itself.

contents.html_ja: 他のインターネットベースのシステムと同様に、DNS はいくつかの脅威にさらされています。これらの脅威に対抗するため、国際標準化団体である Internet Engineering Task Force（IETF）は、DNS からのすべての応答に対して出所認証とデータの完全性を提供する、DNS Security Extensions（DNSSEC）と呼ばれる DNS のセキュリティ確保のための仕様の一式を開発しました。NIST は、国土安全保障省と連携して、2004 年から DNSSEC の展開の推進に積極的に関わってきました。
contents.html: As with other Internet-based systems, DNS is subject to several threats. To counter these threats, the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF)—an international standards body—developed a set of specifications for securing DNS called DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC) to provide origin authentication and data integrity for all responses from the DNS. In partnership with the Department of Homeland Security, NIST has been actively involved in promoting the deployment of DNSSEC since 2004.

contents.html_ja: 無線ネットワークは、有線ネットワークと同じ多くのリスクにさらされているだけでなく、追加のリスクに対しても脆弱です。無線ネットワークは、無線周波数でデータを送信するため、保護されていない限り侵入者に対して開かれています。侵入者はこの開放性を悪用して、システムやサービスにアクセスし、データを破壊または窃取し、ネットワーク帯域を占有して認可された利用者へのサービスを拒否する攻撃を仕掛けてきました。
contents.html: While wireless networks are exposed to many of the same risks as wired networks, they are vulnerable to additional risks as well. Wireless networks transmit data through radio frequencies and are open to intruders unless protected. Intruders have exploited this openness to access systems and services, destroy and steal data, and launch attacks that tie up network bandwidth and deny service to authorized users.

contents.html: This past year, we developed a new Special Publication (SP) dealing with wireless security issues. Draft NIST SP 800-127, Guide to Security for WiMAX Technologies, was published in September 2009. It discusses security considerations for current and past IEEE 802.16 specifications for Worldwide Interoperability for Microwave Access (WiMAX) technologies. WiMAX is a wireless metropolitan area network (WLAN) communications technology that can be used for last-mile broadband access or cellular-like mobile architectures. Draft SP 800-127 explains the security features provided by the IEEE 802.16 standards and provides recommendations to federal agencies on securing their WiMAX technologies. We expect to finalize the publication during FY2010.

contents.html_ja: CS1 の範囲は、現在 INCITS の B10、M1、T3、T10、T11 や、Alliance for Telecommunications Industry Solutions、Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.、Internet Engineering Task Force（IETF）、Travel Industry Association of America、Accredited Standards Committee（ASC）X9 などの他の標準グループで進行中のサイバーセキュリティ標準化の作業分野を、明示的に除外しています。CS1 の作業範囲には、NIST コンピュータセキュリティ部門が扱うのとほぼ同じサイバーセキュリティ分野の標準化が含まれます。
contents.html: The scope of CS1 explicitly excludes the areas of work on cyber security standardization presently underway in INCITS B10, M1, T3, T10 and T11; as well as other standard groups, such as the Alliance for Telecommunications Industry Solutions, the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc., the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF), the Travel Industry Association of America, and Accredited Standards Committee (ASC) X9. The CS1 scope of work includes standardization in most of the same cyber security areas as are covered in the NIST Computer Security Division.

contents.html_ja: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 27 に対する米国の TAG として、CS1 は、IT Security Techniques に関する SC 27 の作業計画に、SC 27 の標準プロジェクトに対する用語、コメント、貢献という形で寄与し、さまざまな開発段階にある SC 27 の標準文書の投票を行い、さまざまな SC 27 のプロジェクトに取り組む、またはさまざまな SC 27 のリーダーシップ職に就く米国の専門家を特定しています。現在、多くの CS1 のメンバーが、さまざまな標準プロジェクトで SC 27 の文書の編集者または共同編集者を務めており、ISO/IEC 24759、Test Requirements for Cryptographic Modules では NIST の Randy Easter が、29150、Signcryption では NIST の Allen Roginsky が共同編集者を務めています。Erika McCallister は、29115、Entity Authentication Assurance の編集者を引き継ぐ予定です。
contents.html: As the U.S. TAG to ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 27, CS1 contributes to the SC 27 program of work on IT Security Techniques in terms, comments, and contributions on SC 27 standards projects; votes on SC 27 standards documents at various stages of development; and identifying U.S. experts to work on various SC 27 projects or to serve in various SC 27 leadership positions. Currently a number of CS1 members are serving as SC 27 document editors or coeditors on various standards projects, including Randy Easter of NIST for ISO/IEC 24759, Test Requirements for Cryptographic Modules, and Allen Roginsky of NIST, Co-Editor on 29150, Signcryption. Erika McCallister will take over as Editor of 29115, Entity Authentication Assurance.

contents.html_ja: CS1 からのすべての入力は、INCITS を通じて ANSI に送られ、その後 SC 27 に届きます。この仕組みは、米国発の新規作業項目提案や米国で策定された国家標準を、国際的な SC 27 の標準策定プロセスに取り込むための経路にもなっています。CS1 は、その国際的な取組において、ISO/IEC JTC1 SC 27 のすべての国際セキュリティ標準プロジェクトに対する貢献の要請に、一貫して、効率的に、タイムリーに対応してきました。加えて CS1 は、SC 27 のいくつかの新しい作業分野に貢献しており、これには、金融・保険サービス向けの情報セキュリティマネジメントのガイドライン、ISO/IEC 20000-1 と ISO/IEC 27001 の統合的な実施に関するガイダンス、Secure System Engineering の原則と技法（Technical report type 2）、軽量暗号、情報セキュリティガバナンス（ISG）フレームワーク、デジタル証拠の識別、収集または取得、保全のガイドライン、アウトソーシングのセキュリティのガイドライン、ID エスクローを伴う相対的匿名性の要件、プライバシー能力成熟度モデルに関する、検討期間または新規作業項目提案が含まれます。
contents.html: All input from CS1 goes through INCITS to ANSI, then to SC 27. This arrangement is also a conduit for getting U.S.-based new work item proposals and U.S.-developed national standards into the international SC 27 standards development process. In its international efforts, CS1 has consistently, efficiently, and in a timely manner responded to all calls for contributions on all international security standards projects in ISO/IEC JTC1 SC 27. In addition CS1 is making contributions on several new areas of work in SC 27, including study periods and/or new work item proposals on Information security management guidelines for financial and insurance services, Guidance on the integrated implementation of ISO/IEC 20000-1 and ISO/IEC 27001, Secure System Engineering principles and techniques (Technical report type 2), Lightweight cryptography, an Information security governance (ISG) framework, Guidelines for identification, collection and/or acquisition and preservation of digital evidence, Guidelines for security of outsourcing, Requirements on relative anonymity with identity escrow, and a Privacy Capability Maturity Model.

contents.html_ja: Dan Benigni が議決権のない議長を務め、Richard Kissel が議決権を持つ NIST の主担当である CS1 への参加を通じて、NIST は、CS1 のすべての国内および国際的な IT セキュリティ標準の取組に貢献しています。国際的には 80 を超える発行済みの標準があり、そのほとんどは国家標準です。現在進行中の国際標準プロジェクトは 63 を超えます。
contents.html: Through its membership on CS1, where Dan Benigni serves as the nonvoting chair, and Richard Kissel is the NIST Primary with vote, NIST contributes to all CS1 national and international IT security standards efforts. Internationally, there are over 80 published standards, and almost all are National Standards. There are more than 63 current international standards projects.

contents.html_ja: CS1 には、Small Organization Baseline Information Security Handbook という名称の国家標準プロジェクトに取り組む臨時グループがあります。CS1 の NIST の主担当メンバーは Richard Kissel で、中小企業とセキュリティの問題についてやり取りしています。彼が最近公開した NISTIR 7621 の草案、Small Business Information Security: The Fundamentals が、この CS1 の国家標準プロジェクトの基礎文書です。この作業は、今後の中小企業に対する NIST のセキュリティのアウトリーチに直接影響を与えます。
contents.html: CS1 has an ad hoc group working on the national standards project titled Small Organization Baseline Information Security Handbook. The NIST Principal member of CS1 is Richard Kissel, who interacts with small business organizations on security issues. His recently released draft NISTIR 7621, Small Business Information Security: The Fundamentals, is the base document for this CS1 national standards project. This work will have a direct impact on NIST’s outreach on security to small and medium sized businesses in future.

contents.html: He is currently a Liaison to the follow-on Phase II "Workshop of The Financial Impact of Cyber Risk- 50 Questions Every CFO Should Ask", a joint initiative to identify and respond to the current needs of the C-suite community regarding cyber risk. While Phase I focused on providing questions that organizations/CFOs should be asking and provided guidance on the identification and quantification of the financial risk associated with cyber security, Phase II focuses on the developing an implementation strategy/process for the Phase I questions. Additionally, this initiative is focusing on filling out that framework to make better informed decisions related to cyber risk from an economic standpoint. The final Workshop framework document from Phase I is available for your review at http://webstore.ansi.org/cybersecurity.

contents.html_ja: NIST SP 800-127、Guide to Security for WiMAX Technologies は、2009 年 9 月にパブリックコメントのために公開されました。Worldwide In-teroperability for Microwave Access（WiMAX）は、IEEE 802.16 標準に基づく無線メトロポリタンエリアネットワークの通信技術です。WiMAX 技術は元々、ラストワンマイルのブロードバンド無線アクセスを提供するために開発されましたが、現在は携帯電話に似たモバイルアーキテクチャにいっそう重点を置いています。SP 800-127 の草案は、WiMAX の基本を説明し、WiMAX のセキュリティ機能に関する情報を提供し、WiMAX 技術を効果的に保護するための推奨事項を示しています。また、IEEE 802.16 標準の主要なバージョン間のセキュリティ上の違いも説明しています。
contents.html: NIST SP 800-127, Guide to Security for WiMAX Technologies, was released for public comment in September 2009. Worldwide In-teroperability for Microwave Access (WiMAX) is a wireless metropolitan area network communications technology based on the IEEE 802.16 standard. WiMAX technologies were originally developed to provide last-mile broadband wireless access, but are now more focused on cellular-like mobile architectures. Draft SP 800-127 explains the basics of WiMAX, provides information on the security capabilities of WiMAX, and gives recommendations on securing WiMAX technologies effectively. It also explains the security differences among the major versions of the IEEE 802.16 standard.

contents.html: NIST SP 800-126, The Technical Specification for the Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP), was released for public comment in July 2009. SP 800-126 provides a technical overview of SCAP, focusing on how software developers can integrate SCAP technology into their product offerings and interfaces.

contents.html_ja: NIST SP 800-124、Guidelines on Cell Phone and PDA Security, は、現在使われている携帯電話と携帯情報端末（PDA）機器の概要を示し、それらの扱いに関して、十分な情報に基づく情報技術セキュリティ上の判断を行うための知見を提供します。SP 800-124 は、これらの機器の使用に伴う脅威と技術的リスク、およびそれらを緩和するために利用できる保護措置の詳細を示しています。組織は、SP 800-124 に示された情報を使って、セキュリティを強化し、携帯電話や PDA 機器に関わるインシデントを減らすことができます。SP 800-124 は 2008 年 10 月に最終版として発行されました。
contents.html: NIST SP 800-124, Guidelines on Cell Phone and PDA Security, provides an overview of cell phone and personal digital assistant (PDA) devices in use today and offers insights into making informed information technology security decisions on their treatment. SP 800-124 gives details about the threats and technology risks associated with the use of these devices and the available safeguards to mitigate them. Organizations can use the information presented in SP 800-124 to enhance security and reduce incidents involving cell phone and PDA devices. SP 800-124 was published as final in October 2008.

contents.html: NIST SP 800-122, Guide to Protecting the Confidentiality of Personally Identifiable Information (PII), was released for public comment in January 2009. SP 800-122 is intended to assist federal organizations in identifying PII and determining what level of protection each instance of PII requires, based on the potential impact of a breach of the PII's confidentiality. The publication also suggests safeguards that may offer appropriate protection for PII and makes recommendations regarding PII data breach handling.

contents.html_ja: NIST SP 800-41 Revision 1、Guidelines on Firewalls and Firewall Policy は、組織がファイアウォール技術とファイアウォールポリシーの能力を理解するのを支援します。ファイアウォールポリシーの策定、およびファイアウォールの選択、構成、試験、展開、管理に関する実用的な推奨事項を提供します。また、ファイアウォールソリューションを選択する際に考慮すべき要因も論じています。2009 年 9 月に最終版として発行されたこの刊行物は、2002 年に公開された SP 800-41 の元の版に置き換わるものです。
contents.html: NIST SP 800-41 Revision 1, Guidelines on Firewalls and Firewall Policy, helps organizations understand the capabilities of firewall technologies and firewall policies. It provides practical recommendations for developing firewall policies and for selecting, configuring, testing, deploying, and managing firewalls. It also discusses factors to consider when selecting firewall solutions. This publication, which was published as final in September 2009, replaces the original version of SP 800-41, which was released in 2002.

contents.html_ja: NISTIR 7517、The Common Misuse Scoring System (CMSS): Metrics for Software Feature Misuse Vulnerabilities は、2009 年 2 月にパブリックコメントのために公開されました。この報告書は、ソフトウェアの機能の悪用の脆弱性の深刻度についての標準化された尺度の一式である CMSS の仕様を提案しています。NISTIR 7517 は、CMSS の尺度とスコアがどのように決定されるかの例も示しています。CMSS が最終化されれば、CMSS のデータは、組織が標準化された定量的な脆弱性データに基づいてセキュリティ上の判断を行うのに役立ちます。
contents.html: NISTIR 7517, The Common Misuse Scoring System (CMSS): Metrics for Software Feature Misuse Vulnerabilities, was released for public comment in February 2009. This report proposes a specification for CMSS, a set of standardized measures for the severity of software feature misuse vulnerabilities. NISTIR 7517 also provides examples of how CMSS measures and scores would be determined. Once CMSS is finalized, CMSS data can assist organizations in making security decisions based on standardized, quantitative vulnerability data.

contents.html: NISTIR 7511, Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP) Validation Program Test Requirements Version 1.1, describes the requirements that must be met by products to achieve SCAP validation. Validation is awarded by independent laboratories that have been accredited for SCAP testing. This report, which was originally released for public comment in August 2008 and updated in April 2009, was written primarily for accredited laboratories and for vendors interested in receiving SCAP validation for their products. A second version of this report, Revision 1, was also released for public comment in April 2009, and it defines a newer set of validation program test requirements.

contents.html_ja: NISTIR 7502、The Common Configuration Scoring System (CCSS): Metrics for Software Security Configuration Vulnerabilities は、2009 年 6 月に第 2 回のパブリックコメント期間のために公開されました。CCSS は、ソフトウェアのセキュリティ構成上の問題の特性と相対的な深刻度を測定し伝達するための、オープンな仕様です。この刊行物は、CCSS の仕様を提案し、スコアリングの実施に関する助言を示し、一連の例を通じて CCSS の使用を実証しています。CCSS の仕様が最終化され、製品の CCSS の尺度が利用できるようになれば、組織は、標準化された定量的な脆弱性データに基づいてセキュリティ上の判断を行うために CCSS を使うことができます。
contents.html: NISTIR 7502, The Common Configuration Scoring System (CCSS): Metrics for Software Security Configuration Vulnerabilities, was released for a second public comment period in June 2009. CCSS is an open specification for measuring and communicating the characteristics and relative severity of software security configuration issues. This publication proposes a specification for CCSS, provides advice on performing scoring, and demonstrates the use of CCSS through a set of examples. Once the CCSS specification has been finalized and CCSS measures for products are available, organizations can use CCSS to help them make security decisions based on standardized, quantitative vulnerability data.

contents.html_ja: リーダーシップ: このグループは、セキュリティ上の欠陥のデータベース（国家脆弱性データベース）、142 件のセキュリティ構成ガイドの集成、脆弱性をスコアリングするための測定指標を含む、コンピュータセキュリティの脆弱性の特定と是正の新しいモデル（セキュリティコンテンツ自動化プロトコル）を先駆的に開発したことで表彰されます。その成果には、米国政府の 500 万台の Windows デスクトップコンピュータの安全な構成の実現、世界中のクレジットカード取引のセキュリティ向上、業界のセキュリティツールが安全な構成を効果的に監視し実施できるようにしたことが含まれます。
contents.html: Leadership: The group is honored for pioneering a new model for computer security vulnerability identification and remediation (the Security Content Automation Protocol), including a database of security flaws (the National Vulnerability Database), a compendium of 142 security configuration guides, and metrics for scoring vulnerabilities. Their accomplishments include enabling the secure configuration of 5 million U.S. Government Windows desktop computers, increasing the security of credit card transactions worldwide, and enabling industry security tools to effectively monitor and implement secure configurations.

contents.html_ja: Ms. Scarfone は、世界最大かつ最も影響力のあるコンピュータセキュリティガイドラインの 1 つの策定を主導したことで表彰されます。彼女の執筆とリーダーシップにより、これらの刊行物の策定は、量、品質、影響の面で新たな高みに達しました。これらのガイドラインは連邦機関が使うために作成されたものですが、非政府組織も頻繁に採用し適用しています。各特別刊行物は、特定の情報技術の話題に関連する新たな脅威と既存の脅威を緩和するための、実行可能な推奨事項を提供することで、何らかの形で政府のセキュリティ態勢を直接向上させています。
contents.html: Ms. Scarfone is recognized for leading the development of one of the world’s largest and most influential of computer security guidelines. Her authorship and leadership have taken the development of these publications to new heights in terms of volume, quality, and impact. Although prepared for use by federal agencies, these guidelines are also frequently adopted and applied by nongovernmental organizations. Each Special Publication in some way directly improves the security posture of our government by providing actionable recommendations for mitigating emerging and existing threats that pertain to a specific information technology topic.

contents.html: The Western Hemisphere Travel Initiative requires all travelers from Canada, Mexico, Central America, South America, the Caribbean and Bermuda to present acceptable documents to enter the U.S. The U.S. Passport Card (PASS Card) was a proposed alternative to the passport. Congress asked NIST to certify that the Department of Homeland Security and State selected a PASS Card architecture that met or exceeded ISO security standards and the best available practices for protection of personal identification documents. The NIST team met the Congressional mandate, improved the security, durability, and performance of the PASS Card, and enabled the State Department to issue the PASS Cards almost a full year before the planned implementation date.
contents.html_ja: 西半球旅行イニシアチブ（Western Hemisphere Travel Initiative）は、カナダ、メキシコ、中央アメリカ、南アメリカ、カリブ海諸国、バミューダからのすべての旅行者に対し、米国に入国するために認められた書類の提示を求めています。米国パスポートカード（PASS カード）は、パスポートの代替として提案されたものでした。議会は NIST に対し、国土安全保障省と国務省が、個人識別書類の保護に関する ISO のセキュリティ標準と利用可能な最良の実践を満たすか上回る PASS カードのアーキテクチャを選択したことを認証するよう求めました。NIST のチームは議会の義務付けを満たし、PASS カードのセキュリティ、耐久性、性能を改善し、国務省が計画された実施日のほぼ丸 1 年前に PASS カードを発行できるようにしました。

contents.html: Matthew Barrett, Computer Security Division, received the 2009 Federal 100 Award from Federal Computer Week. contents.html_ja: コンピュータセキュリティ部門の Karen Scarfone は、Federal Computer Week から 2009 年 Federal 100 Award を受賞しました。Federal 100 Award は、2008 年に連邦の情報技術コミュニティに大きく貢献した、政府と産業界の個人を表彰するものです。Scarfone は、インシデント対応、ホストのセキュリティ、モバイル機器とテレワークのセキュリティに関する、比類のないセキュリティ刊行物群を策定した執筆とリーダーシップを評価されました。賞は、2009 年 3 月 25 日にバージニア州 Tysons Corner の Ritz-Carlton Hotel で開かれた祝賀会で授与されました。
contents.html: Karen Scarfone, Computer Security Division, received the 2009 Federal 100 Award from Federal Computer Week. The Federal 100 Award recognizes individuals in government and industry who made significant contributions to the federal information technology community in 2008. Scarfone was recognized for authorship and leadership in developing an unparalleled corpus of security publications on incident response, host security, and mobile device and telework security. The award was presented at a gala at the Ritz-Carlton Hotel in Tysons Corner, Virginia, on March 25, 2009.

contents.html: Opportunities are available at NIST for 6- to 24-month internships within CSD. Generally speaking, the salary costs are borne by the sponsoring institution; however, in some cases, these guest research internships carry a small monthly stipend paid by NIST. For further information, contact Mr. Curt Barker, (301) 975-8443, william.barker@nist.gov or Ms. Donna Dodson, (301) 975-3669, donna.dodson@nist.gov.

contents.html_ja: NIST は、さまざまな方法で産業界と学界の研究に資金を提供しています。Technology Innovation Program は、NIST が技術的に得意とする分野で、国家と社会の重要なニーズに対応する、革命的となり得る技術の研究に対して、産業界、大学、コンソーシアムに費用分担型の賞を提供しています。Small Business Innovation Research Program は、中小企業からの研究開発の提案に資金を提供しています。また、精密測定、火災研究、材料科学といった特定の分野での取組を奨励するために、その他の助成金も提供しています。産業界、学界、その他の機関での研究を支援する助成金／賞は、研究所のいくつかの異なる部署を通じて、競争ベースで利用できます。NIST の助成金プログラムに関する一般的な情報は、Ms. Melinda Chukran（(301) 975-5266、melinda.chukran@nist.gov）にお問い合わせください。
contents.html: NIST funds industrial and academic research in a variety of ways. Our Technology Innovation Program provides cost-shared awards to industry, universities, and consortia for research on potentially revolutionary technologies that address critical national and societal needs in NIST’s areas of technical competence. The Small Business Innovation Research Program funds R&D proposals from small businesses. We also offer other grants to encourage work in specific fields: precision measurement, fire research, and materials science. Grants/awards supporting research at industry, academia, and other institutions are available on a competitive basis through several different Institute offices. For general information on NIST grants programs, contact Ms. Melinda Chukran, (301) 975-5266, melinda.chukran@nist.gov.

contents.html: Here’s your chance to satisfy that curiosity, by spending part of your summer working elbow-to-elbow with researchers at NIST, one of the world’s leading research organizations and home to three Nobel Prize winners. Gain valuable hands-on experience, work with cutting-edge technology, meet peers from across the nation (from San Francisco to Puerto Rico, New York to New Mexico), and sample the Washington, D.C., area. And get paid while you're learning. For further information, see http://www.surf.nist.gov or contact NIST SURF Program, 100 Bureau Dr., Stop 8400, Gaithersburg, MD 20899-8499, (301) 975-4200, NIST_SURF_program@nist.gov.

Chief Cybersecurity Advisor

In FY2009, CSD continued to develop cybersecurity standards, se curity metrics, and product assurance programs to promote, mea sure, and validate the security attributes of information systems and services. As technology advances and security requirements evolve, CSD critically evaluates existing standards, guidelines, and technologies to ensure that they adequately reflect the current state of the art. In FY2009, CSD published revisions of The Digital SignatureStandard,FederalInformationProcessingStandard(FIPS) 198-1 and SecureHashStandard, FIPS 180-3, published twelve final and twelve draft security guidelines in the form of NIST Special Publications, and drafted ten Interagency Reports on cybersecu rity topics. During FY2009 CSD continued its national and inter national consensus standards activities, particularly in the areas of cryptographic functions, cryptographic product assurance, and identity credentials. Also during FY2009, CSD continued its inter national competition for a next generation Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA-3) and continued to expand its support for sector-specific national initiatives: electronic voting, Smart Grid, and health infor mation technology.

The Computer Security Division (CSD), a component of NIST’s Information Technology Laboratory (ITL), provides standards and technology to protect information systems against threats to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and services. During Fiscal Year 2009 (FY2009), CSD continued its standards development and cybersecurity outreach activities and carried out an expanded research agenda designed to develop and implement high-quality, cost-effective mechanisms needed to improve information security and privacy across the federal government and throughout the national and international information security community. CSD worked with federal partners to establish a unified framework for information security across the federal government. This initiative is resulting in greater standardization and more consistent and cost-effective security for all federal information systems.

original_blocks.html: To better assist the Nation in meeting its ever-increasing cybersecurity needs, in FY2009 CSD became more tightly integrated into both ITL and Department of Commerce cybersecurity activities. CSD provided a Chief Cybersecurity Advisor to the Director of ITL and a cybersecurity coordinator for the Department of Commerce Cybersecurity and Privacy Task Force. These new roles were necessary to better coordinate NIST and Commerce participation in inter-departmental cybersecurity planning and to more effectively leverage the resources necessary to make significant contributions to Departmental and National initiatives. CSD also led ITL’s transition from planning for Comprehensive National Cybersecurity Initiative (CNCI) activities to initiation of CNCI research programs and implementation of recommendations of the President’s 2009 Cyberspace Policy Review.

original_blocks.html: The 2009 FISSEA conference was held at NIST on March 24-26, 2009. Approximately 170 information systems security professionals and trainers attended, primarily from federal agencies, but including college and university faculty and staff, and industry representatives from firms that support federal information systems and security programs.The theme was“Awareness,Training, and Education –The Catalyst for Organizational Change.” Conference attendees were given the opportunity to tour NIST and participate in a vendor exhibition. FISSEA conferences provide a great networking opportunity for attendees. The 2010 conference will be held at the National Institutes of Health on March 23-25 and the theme is “Unraveling the Enigma of Role-Based Training”. The first two days of the 3-day conference include one track devoted to role-based training and a second track focusing on awareness, training, education, and certification topics. The third day features a special emphasis on Cyber Security Initiatives. Captain Cheryl Seaman is the Conference Director and Daniel Benjamin is the Program Director. Further information regarding the conference is available on the FISSEA website.

original_blocks.html: The Information Security and Privacy Advisory Board (ISPAB) is a federal advisory committee that brings together senior professionals from industry, government, and academia to help advise NIST, the U.S. Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the Secretary of Commerce, and appropriate committees of the U.S. Congress about information security and privacy issues pertaining to unclassified federal government information systems.

original_blocks.html: The Cryptographic Module Validation Program (CMVP) and the Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program (CAVP) were developed by NIST to support the needs of the user community for strong, independently tested and commercially available cryptographic products. Through these programs, NIST works with the commercial sector and the cryptographic community to achieve security, interoperability, and assurance. The goal of these programs is to promote the use of validated products and provide federal agencies with a security metric to use in procuring cryptographic modules. The testing performed by accredited laboratories provides this metric. Federal agencies, industry, and the public can choose cryptographic modules and/ or products containing cryptographic modules from the CMVP Validated Modules List and have confidence in the claimed level of security.

original_blocks.html: Vendors of cryptographic modules and algorithms use independent, private sector testing laboratories accredited as CST laboratories by NVLAP to have their cryptographic modules validated by the CMVP and their cryptographic algorithms validated by the CAVP. As the worldwide growth and use of cryptographic modules has increased, demand to meet the testing needs for both algorithms and modules developed by vendors has also grown. There are currently 18 accredited laboratories in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Germany, Spain, Japan, and Taiwan R.O.C. NVLAP has received several applications for the accreditation of CST Laboratories, both domestically and internationally. A complete list of accredited laboratories may be found at http://csrc.nist.gov/groups/STM/testing_labs/.

original_blocks.html: The CMVP and the CAVP are separate, collaborative programs based on a partnership between NIST’s CSD and the Communication Security Establishment Canada (CSEC). The programs provide federal agencies—in the United States and Canada—confidence that a validated cryptographic module meets a claimed level of security assurance and that a validated cryptographic algorithm has been implemented correctly. The CMVP and the CAVP validate modules and algorithms used in a wide variety of products, including secure Internet browsers, secure radios, smart cards, space-based communications, munitions, security tokens, storage devices, and products supporting Public Key Infrastructure and electronic commerce. One module may be used in several products, so a small number of modules may account for hundreds of products. Likewise, the CAVP validates cryptographic algorithms that may be integrated in one or more cryptographic modules.

original_blocks.html: The CMVP and the CAVP have stimulated improved quality and security assurance of cryptographic modules. Statistics from the testing laboratories show that 60 percent of the cryptographic modules and 9 percent of the cryptographic algorithms brought in for voluntary testing had security flaws that were corrected during testing. Without this program, the federal government would have had less than a 50 percent chance of buying correctly implemented cryptography. To date, over 1,185 validation certificates have been issued, representing over 2,420 modules that were validated by the CMVP. These modules have been developed by more than 280 domestic and international vendors.

NISTIR 7621, Small Business Information Security: The Fundamentals

NIST, in partnership with the Small Business Administration and the Federal Bureau of Investigation has had educational outreach to the small business community since 2002. With full participa tion from our partners, we schedule, promote, and conduct infor mation security workshops for small businesses throughout the United States.

The core information in the workshops has been collected in NISTIR 7621, Small Business Information Security: The Fundamen tals. This document covers the fundamentals of information security for small business. The intent was to publish a short, easy to read document that small business owners could use to protect the information, computers, and networks used in their small businesses.
The draft of NISTIR 7621 was released for public comment in Sep tember 2009 and is planned for release as a final document in the first quarter of FY2010.
